will find the lowest areas. Indeed that is what happened. Propane obviously got into the home, how and why, we are still trying to determine that. And it caused a flammable atmosphere. you have two dogs, three cats, you know that your priority is to get your pets out of the home. I always urge you to get yourself out. They were in the basement of the home looking for their animals. happened within the range. An ignition can ignite, and the explosion occurred. Subsequently, you have all seen the pictures. The house was 100% level. to go into the mode of rescuing multiple firefighters who were trapped inside, as well as the numerous ones on the outside. Our crews asked for help from the team, and then the battalion chief was added to this winter three alarms, and numerous units. I believe that it was over 100 units that were on the scene at some point, during this event. During the entire event. And ultimately, immediately, we determined that one firefighter, trevor brown , was found on the scene

deceased, there was no resuscitation efforts. It was immediately determined that he was deceased on the scene, but nevertheless, they went into the mode of rescuing at least two firefighters who were trapped. I was asking this morning, I do not believe that we have any statistics on the survival rate of firefighters calling mayday who are trapped, we rescued those two as well as everybody else. To

make a long story short, we ended up with 14 incidents. the burn center. They remained there. Most likely, a short statement the firefighter from sterling, who received first and second degree burns to himself, he has a longer road to recovery, for sure. of them, to check in and see how they were doing. Including the ones that are in the hospitals. For that matter, they were all positive. They are all doing better, and the majority of those injuries, including firefighter brown, he was outside the home, when he got killed. He was not inside. He was not in the basement or anything like that. So, we often think of the outside of the home as our safe refuge area, certainly this did not prove, in fact, to be a safe refuge. And so, the folks are heavily engaged. You know, and

we have probably heard about this, but we have been with it for the entire time of this and that. This was the first time, and came to work, and that was a real job. people in general. It is enormous. I know that you appreciate that, chair randall. of work that has to be done. Certainly at county hr and risk management, they have been assisting us greatly. First and foremost, our priority has been taking care of our people. niosh entity, that is not an enforcement arm, they will provide recommendations for things that we did better, things that we could do right in this incident.
